videos.title: Why slides are not a script
Six principles of a video lesson

slides.narration:

slides.narration:
By the end of this lesson you can do four things.
Name the six principles of a video lesson.
Spot the open, the body and the close in any script.
Write a five to ten minute script for your own lesson.
And check that script against a ten-point list before you record.

slides.narration:
Three parts.
We start with the six principles.

slides.label: Part 1
slides.title: Six principles of a video lesson
slides.subtitle: Each one comes with a warning sign you can spot yourself
slides.narration:
Part one.
Six principles.
For each one I give you a warning sign, so you can check your own videos.

slides.label: Part 1
slides.title: Six principles of a video lesson

cards.title: One video, one idea
cards.text: Under ten minutes, its own open and close

cards.title: Show, don't read
cards.text: Never read the slide out loud

cards.title: Point at the key part
cards.text: Circle, zoom, highlight as you speak

cards.title: Learners must act
cards.text: A question and a pause in each video

slides.narration:
Here are the six.
One video teaches one idea.
Pictures add to your words, they do not repeat them.
Cut everything that does not serve the objective.
Point at exactly what you are talking about.
Talk to one person, as if they were sitting next to you.
And make the learner do something, not just listen.
slides.notes: Reveal the cards one by one with the narration.

slides.label: Part 1 · Two clips
slides.title: Two clips, same content

left.title: Clip A
items: Nine lines of text, read aloud
Background music and fly-ins
Talks to a crowd
No question at all

right.title: Clip B
items: One line and one simple diagram
The pointer lands on the right spot
Says you, tells a story
Stops for a pause question

slides.narration:
You just watched two clips.
What does clip A have that clip B does not?
A wall of text read word for word, music, fly-ins, and not one question.
Clip B is the opposite.
One idea, a picture that adds to the words, and a pause where you have to think.

slides.label: Part 1 · Evidence
slides.title: Learners who act remember more
slides.takeaway: Hear and see stops at fifty. To reach ninety, give learners something to do.
slides.narration:
Look at the last column.
Only listening, people keep about twenty percent.
Listening and watching, fifty.
Doing something with it, ninety.
So what is your video asking the learner to do?
slides.notes: Columns appear left to right with the narration; the highlighted column appears on the word ninety.

slides.label: Part 2
slides.title: Open, body, close
slides.subtitle: The shape of one video
slides.narration:
Part two.
The shape of a single video.

slides.label: Part 2 · Structure
slides.title: The open: three jobs in thirty seconds
items: Hook: a mistake everyone makes
Promise: what you can do by the end
Route: the two or three stops ahead
slides.narration:
The open has three jobs, and thirty seconds to do them.
A hook, a mistake everyone makes, so the learner wants to keep watching.
A promise, what they can do by the end of the video.
And the route, the two or three stops ahead.
No long hello. No life story.

slides.label: Part 2 · Structure
slides.title: How the time splits
rows: Two to four ideas, each with an example and a pause
Three takeaways, one action, a bridge to the next video
slides.narration:
Here is how the time splits.
The open takes about ten percent.
The body takes three quarters, two to four ideas, each with an example and a pause.
The close takes the last fifteen percent, three takeaways and one thing to do next.

slides.label: Part 3
slides.title: Six steps to a video script
slides.narration:
Part three.
Six steps to a finished script.

slides.label: Part 3 · Process
slides.title: Six steps to a script
slides.narration:
Six steps.
Fix the objective in one sentence.
Cut the lesson into eight to fifteen segments.
Write what you will say, in spoken words.
Pair each segment with one slide.
Add at least two pauses where the learner does something.
Then read it out loud and time it.
slides.notes: Reveal each step with its arrow as the narration reaches it.

slides.label: Quick check
slides.question: Your script runs twelve minutes when you read it aloud. What do you do?
options: Talk faster to fit ten minutes
Cut content or split it into two videos
Keep it, twelve minutes is fine
slides.narration:
Quick check.
Your script runs twelve minutes when you read it aloud.
What do you do?
Pause the video and pick one, thirty seconds.
slides.notes: Silence 3 seconds, then circle answer B.

slides.label: Remember
slides.message:
Over ten minutes? Cut,
do not talk faster.
slides.subtitle: Speed loses the learner; cutting keeps the objective.
slides.narration:
The answer is B.
Over ten minutes, cut or split the video.
Talking faster only loses the learner.

items: One idea per video, pictures add to words
Hook in thirty seconds, example in the body, action at the close
A script is done only when read aloud and checked
slides.narration:
Three keywords for this lesson.
Six principles: one idea per video, and pictures that add to your words.
Open, body, close: a hook in thirty seconds, an example in the body, an action at the close.
Read it aloud: a script is done only when you have read it out loud and checked it.
Remember those three and you can write your first script tonight.
